title: Sable and the Confession
premise: True-crime podcaster Dominic Montrose takes on the 1994 disappearance of Sable Wren, a seventeen-year-old who vanished from the coastal town of Grayhollow, only to discover her diary in an estate sale — with entries continuing for two years after the date she supposedly died. Following the diary's coded references, Dominic uncovers a ring of townspeople who helped Sable fake her death to escape an abuser, protected ever since by a pact of silence. But someone else knows Sable lived: the man she fled, now a respected judge, who has been quietly eliminating witnesses as Dominic's episodes air. The trail ends at a lighthouse cottage where an aging Sable has been hiding in plain sight; she must choose between lifelong anonymity and testifying, and Dominic must choose between closing the case and protecting the found family that survival built.
about_author: Ines Ishikawa is a former court stenographer from Monterey who spent a decade transcribing small-town trials before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about ordinary people forced to become their own justice system.

chapters.title: The Coldest Case
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. In their cramped studio, Dominic introduces the Grayhollow case on air: Sable Wren, seventeen, vanished in 1994, body never found, file closed in under a week. The episode closes with a plea for tips. Emotional beat: restless ambition — Dominic needs one impossible case to prove they can close anything.

chapters.title: Estate Sale, Box Nine
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A listener emails about a box of Sable's belongings sold at an estate auction. Among them: her diary. The final entry is dated fourteen months after her disappearance — and it isn't grief; it's grocery lists. Emotional beat: vertigo, the floor dropping out of a solved story.

chapters.title: Ink That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, with diary excerpts interleaved. Forensic document examiner Marta Okafor confirms the ink and handwriting are period-authentic. Either an elaborate forgery or Sable Wren wrote her own ghost story. Emotional beat: obsession kindling into fire.

chapters.title: Grayhollow Welcomes You
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. They arrive in Grayhollow, a town preserved like a diorama. Interviews with retired Sheriff Dell Hargrove yield rehearsed answers and one slip: he calls Sable 'that poor girl' before anyone mentioned her name. Emotional beat: the uncanny politeness of people guarding something.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Waited
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Theo Marsh, now fifty, runs the bait shop where teenage Sable once worked. He recognizes the podcast voice immediately but says nothing. Flashback threads show young Theo burning a letter the night she vanished. Emotional beat: thirty years of guilt compressed into a smile.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Decoding the diary's later entries reveals place names: the quarry, the chapel ruins, 'the Judge's boat.' Each maps to real Grayhollow locations — and each was searched in 1994 by people who apparently already knew what they'd find. Emotional beat: the map turning inside out.

chapters.title: Judge Ambrose Vail
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic interviews Vail, now circuit judge, whose brother Raymond was Sable's employer and the last person to see her. Vail is charming, generous, and asks one question too precisely: 'Where exactly did you acquire this diary?' Emotional beat: cold water down the spine.

chapters.title: What Theo Buried
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Dominic corners Theo at the dock. He confesses fragments: Sable came to him bruised and terrified the summer of '94; Raymond Vail had been hurting her for a year, and no one — not police, not church, not parents — believed her. Emotional beat: shame finally given somewhere to go.

chapters.title: A Death, Manufactured
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, flashback-heavy. The reconstruction: Sable's bicycle at the cliff road, shoes on the rocks, a staged drowning arranged by a handful of believers — Theo, Dell Hargrove, the ferryman Cole Ives, and Sable herself. She rowed out to a waiting trawler. Emotional beat: terrible tenderness; a crime committed as mercy.

chapters.title: Then Who Kept Writing?
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. If Sable left in '94, the post-disappearance diary entries mean she returned — repeatedly, secretly, until 1996. Someone in town was feeding her information, leaving the diary for her. Dominic suspects Theo; Theo swears it wasn't him. Emotional beat: the mystery doubling beneath itself.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Silence
chapters.summary: Cole Ives's POV. The old ferryman, dying of emphysema, listens to Dominic's third episode in his hospital room. He sends a note: 'Ask about the winter trips.' He dies before Dominic can visit. His note is found torn in half. Emotional beat: dread arriving ahead of evidence.

chapters.title: Raymond's Ledger
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Digging into Raymond Vail's estate, Dominic finds shipping ledgers showing his fishing charter made unlogged night runs for two years after Sable's death — the same window as the diary. Raymond wasn't searching for her. He was hunting. Emotional beat: the predator revealed to have never stopped.

chapters.title: Episode Seven Goes Wrong
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic airs the ledger findings. Within hours, Marta Okafor's office is burglarized — the diary's authentication report stolen. Then Theo's bait shop burns. No one is hurt, which is the message. Emotional beat: the case reaching back and touching everyone who helped.

chapters.title: The Pact
chapters.summary: Dell Hargrove's POV. The retired sheriff, wracked by the arson, breaks: he explains the pact — five sworn to protect Sable, meeting yearly, keeping her return visits secret even from each other's knowledge. But one member stopped attending in 2011: Judge Ambrose Vail's clerk, Ruth Calloway. Emotional beat: a wall cracking from the inside.

chapters.title: Ruth Calloway's Drawer
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Ruth, still employed at the courthouse, kept copies of everything: Raymond's sealed juvenile records, a restraining order Sable filed at sixteen and withdrew under pressure, and letters — Sable's letters, sent through Ruth until 1996, then silence. Emotional beat: bureaucratic paper revealed as an act of love.

chapters.title: Winter Trips
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV, flashback. The truth of the diary: Sable came back every winter for two years, hidden in Ruth's attic, gathering documents against Raymond — building a case no one would hear. When Raymond drowned in a boating accident in 1996, Sable left for good, taking the diary's first half and leaving the rest behind by mistake. Emotional beat: grief for a justice that almost arrived.

chapters.title: The Accident Wasn't
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Cross-referencing tide charts and the coroner's thin file, Dominic concludes Raymond's death coincided with one of Sable's winter visits — and that Ambrose Vail has suspected for thirty years that his brother's death wasn't accidental. He hasn't been erasing witnesses to hide a murder. He's been hunting the woman he believes murdered his brother. Emotional beat: the hunter and hunted swapping masks.

chapters.title: Run, Podcaster
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Vail confronts Dominic directly — not with threats, but with a warrant application, defamation filings, and a quiet offer: hand over the diary, drop the series, leave Grayhollow. Dominic records the conversation. That night their rental car's brakes fail on the cliff road. They survive by inches. Emotional beat: fear sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse Cottage
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, first time. Now sixty miles north, living as 'Marion Ashe,' a lighthouse caretaker, Sable has listened to every episode. She drives to Grayhollow and finds Dominic bruised and stubborn. She tells them everything face to face — and says she will never testify, because the law failed her once and she doesn't intend to let it try again. Emotional beat: two survivors of different storms recognizing each other.

chapters.title: What Justice Costs
chapters.summary: Sable and Dominic's alternating POV. Dominic argues the case isn't hers alone anymore — Theo, Dell, Ruth all risked everything and are being picked off. Sable realizes her silence, once armor, has become their exposure. She agrees to go public, but on her terms: her own recording, her own words, released whether or not the courts act. Emotional beat: the price of survival finally itemized and accepted.

chapters.title: The Confession
chapters.summary: Climax. Dominic's POV. The final episode airs: Sable's full account, unedited, alongside the documents Ruth preserved. Vail moves to have it suppressed; instead it detonates nationally. Confronted at the courthouse steps by reporters and by Ruth's evidence, Vail's composure shatters — he admits he'd hired men to frighten witnesses, believing Sable killed Raymond. Arrested, ruined, he whispers the question he's carried thirty years: 'Did she?' Dominic lets the recording answer. Emotional beat: catharsis without neatness.

chapters.title: After the Last Entry
chapters.summary: Resolution, Sable's POV. Months later: Vail awaits trial; Theo rebuilds the shop with unexpected help; Dell tends Sable's mother's grave, finally able to say where she went. Sable signs her own name for the first time in decades on a lease in Grayhollow. Dominic closes the series with the diary's true final entry — written yesterday. Emotional beat: a found family assembling itself around a table, alive and accounted for.
